title: The Smell of Soup and the Sound of Money

keywords: the smell of soup and the sound of money
full_text:
One chilly winter afternoon in the bustling marketplace of Aksehir, a poor, shivering traveler walked past the steaming kitchen of a wealthy restaurant. The tavern master was boiling a giant cauldron of fragrant lamb broth seasoned with garlic, cinnamon, and cumin.

The penniless traveler pulled a dry crust of barley bread from his pocket and held it over the fragrant steam rising from the pot. He turned the bread around, inhaled the mouth-watering aroma deeply, and ate his softened crust with immense satisfaction.

Just as the poor man was about to walk away, the greedy restaurant owner leaped out of the shop, seized him by the collar, and roared: "Pay me five copper coins this instant!"

"For what, sir?" gasped the bewildered traveler. "I took not a single drop of your soup!"

"You nourished your bread with my rich steam!" barked the merchant. "The aroma belongs to my cauldron, and you have consumed its goodness!"

A crowd gathered, arguing loudly, when Mulla Nasruddin arrived riding his little gray donkey. Hearing the dispute, Nasruddin stroked his beard solemnly and announced: "Step aside, citizens! I shall adjudicate this case of high culinary jurisprudence!"

Nasruddin turned to the restaurant owner: "Is it true that this man ate the steam of your soup?"
"It is entirely true, Mulla!" cried the shopkeeper eagerly. "And steam costs good money to produce!"

Nasruddin reached deep into his pocket and pulled out five copper coins. He cupped the coins tightly inside his hands and shook them vigorously right next to the tavern master's ear: Jingle, jingle, clink!

"Do you hear that sound, tavern master?" asked Nasruddin with a serious frown.
"Of course I hear it, Mulla!" replied the greedy man. "What of it?"

"The judgment is settled!" proclaimed Nasruddin, pocketing the coins once more. "The sound of money pays in full for the smell of soup. Case dismissed!"

The crowd burst into uproarious laughter, while the greedy merchant slunk back into his shop, thoroughly outwitted by the Mulla's impeccable justice.
moral: A frivolous claim based on thin air deserves to be paid with nothing more than sound.
